items.title: Rufus Reid interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, GA, January 4, 2013
items.q: I mean I could never play some of the things that John Coltrane, that we’ve grown to love, the “Giant Steps” and all that stuff

ctx.x: Well I mean generally the pianists are the ones that — we hope one of us knows the song. But I learned when the piano players knew it and they would — a really good pianist, particularly coming from that ilk of players, the Jimmy Rowles, the Hank Jones, the Tommy Flanagans, they could lead me, if I could see their hands, they could lead me by watching. I also learned the piano a little bit more because now I started really watching so I knew the names of the notes really well. But then they would just lead me.…

knew where the bridge went, at least I got the door. And then I had to retain that. So that is something that is a skill through repetition, but you have to retain it. And that’s what I think the jazz musicians have sensitized those areas, to retain things that just happen. And how can you somehow develop that. And of course there are different levels of how that comes to you. I mean I could never play some of the things that John Coltrane, that we’ve grown to love, the “Giant Steps” and all that stuff, I mean…

Is some of that, when you’re talking about your ears are getting bigger and they’re telling you where to go, is it also some of that like almost attached to your left hand? Like okay I hear this coming and I know that boom, that’s a string down and down a position or something.
